experiment.description: RF-11, round 1 (head-on): the rules behind how LLM agents resolved head-on meetings in a corridor, extracted three times from RF-30's pooled design sessions, each with references, debrief support and a held-out fidelity score.

encounter_descriptions.head_on: Two people walk towards each other along a corridor, on the same line or nearly so (the geometry: their walking lines aligned, or 20 cm apart). Each must get past the other.

resolution_gate.reason: Step 1 asks whether LLM agents can resolve the conflict on their own plans, so the gate is the plan_only rate (ORCA does not steer the pair apart), pooled over the design's 192 sessions of 32 cells x 2 geometries x 3 conditions (exact repeats and counterfactual pairs left out, so each cell counts once per geometry and condition). 0.50 means the plans resolve the meeting more often than not; it is a judgement, not a sourced number. Head-on walkers in life almost never collide, so 0.50 is lenient against people, and strict against plain ORCA here, which passes within the near-miss distance and never counts as resolved (RF-9: 0 of 72). RF-9's pilot resolved 0.24 before resolve_v6's fixes, so failing the gate is a possible Step 1 result.
